newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: OPPOSITION CALL FOR PM TO COUNTERACT BAD PRESS IN ASIA
Federal Opposition leader Kim Beazley says the Australian Government must act to counteract the bad publicity it's getting in Asia.
He says Australia is receiving the worst press coverage in Asia that it's ever had.
Mr Beazley says the Prime Minister has reportedly been criticised in Thailand's two most important influential English language daily newspapers.
One paper has accused Mr Howard of pandering to fringe MP's and bigots for political advantage.
Mr Beazley says the forthcoming bi-partisan motion on immigration and Aboriginal reconciliation will contribute to dealing with the problem.
MELBOURNE CUP HOPES GO THROUGH THEIR PACES
Several of the top fancies for next week's Melbourne Cup have shown impressive form on the track at this morning's breakfast with the stars.
Saintly galloped well, and jockey Darren Beadman says the horse is in good shape for his November campaign, which includes the Melbourne and Japan Cups.
Gai Waterhouse was happy with the form of Nothin' Leica Dane, but warned Oscar Schindler would be the one to beat.
And Lee Freedman says last year's winner, Doriemus is doing everything right in his campaign.
RACISM COMMENTS ENDANGER SA TUNA INDUSTRY
It's claimed the racism debate is jeopardising a South Australian export industry.
This follows comments made by the Mayor of Port Lincoln, Peter Davis, including assertions that mixed race marriages produce mongrel offspring.
A fishing industry official says it will take years to live down damage caused to the Japanese tuna market.
President of the Tuna Boat Owners' Association, Brian Jeffries, says many of the twelve-hundred jobs in the tuna industry could be put in jeopardy.
CLAIMS SUPER LEAGUE INTERNATIONAL SERIES IN DISARRAY
Super League officials have denied suggestions that their plans for international rugby league are already in disarray.
This follows claims the British Lions team, currently touring the Pacific, is stone broke...and being forced to live from hand to mouth.
Team manager Graham Lowe says he has not been able to pay the players' wages and had to lend the an injured player the fare to fly home.

Super League's media office in Sydney says the tour was arranged before the formation of Super League's new international board, and has no bearing on plans for the next year's Australia-Great Britain series.
INVESTIGATION INTO DEATH OF DIPLOMAT'S SON
Australian Federal Police in Canberra are preparing a report for the Coroner following the death of an Indonesian diplomat's son in a car accident.
Raynold Lekapompessy died on Sunday night when the vehicle he was in hit a light pole and bridge support.
A spokesman for the Indonesian Embassy in Canberra says the 20 year old died while out with his family, including his father Frederick, a third secretary with the Embassy.
Mr Lekampompessy, his wife and daughter were taken to hospital suffering minor injuries.
Police have been seeking witnesses to the accident in Yarralumla, but refuse to comment because they are preparing a report for the ACT coroner.
SIGNIFICANT HISTORICAL REMAINS ARRIVING IN TASMANIA
An emotional time is in store for Tasmania's aboriginal community today.
A group of aborigines is due in Hobart this afternoon with aboriginal remains from museums and institutions in New Zealand, Canberra and South Australia.
The secretary of the Tasmanian Aboriginal Centre, Annette Peardon says the remains are among the most significant ever recovered.
CALLS FOR POLLIES' WAGES TO BE LINKED TO JOBS GROWTH
Unions in Tasmania says politicians should only get wage increases if the state's economy grows.
The Manufacturing Workers Union's Tom Harding says State MPs should only receive a flow-on from Federal pay rises if Tasmania is in line with the national average for GDP and unemployment.
Mr Harding also says Tasmania should have only 35 politicians against the present 54, covered by an enterprise agreement.
-- Reuters Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
